channel.title: The RigSight log
channel.description: Notes from building RigSight, a free PC monitor for Windows.

item.title: Riggy, the helper I shipped and removed two days later
item.description: The first try at letting you ask RigSight questions. It was clever, it was careful, and it wasn't really AI. So it went.

item.title: Bugs that make no noise
item.description: Internet use that silently stopped being recorded, an app 'updated' 45 minutes early, and a game 'installed' ten minutes into a 55 GB download.

item.title: My PC wasn't losing power in its sleep
item.description: RigSight said my PC kept losing power while asleep. It didn't. I had misread a number in Windows' own crash record.

item.title: How light is light? Measuring an app that never closes
item.description: Someone suggested rewriting RigSight's sensor reading in C++. Measuring first showed where the time really goes, and that I had read the wrong memory number.

item.title: The day RigSight told me my healthy fan was clogged
item.description: A warning that compared a resting PC with a gaming one, and the rule it left behind. Compare like with like, or say nothing.

item.title: Getting numbers inside a fullscreen game
item.description: Why a normal window can't draw over some games, how RivaTuner gets around it, and the see-through panel that turned solid black.

item.title: Day one, and 25 versions before midnight
item.description: The first public day of RigSight, what it set out to do, and the first mistake it shipped, which counted the page file as RAM.
